questions.questionEn: In pharmacology, what does pharmacokinetics primarily study?
questions.questionZh: 药理学里，pharmacokinetics 主要研究什么？

options.zh: 药物对机体产生什么作用
options.en: What the drug does to the body
The color of the drug packaging

options.zh: 机体如何吸收、分布、代谢和排泄药物
options.en: How the body absorbs, distributes, metabolizes, and eliminates a drug

questions.explanationEn: Pharmacokinetics focuses on ADME: absorption, distribution, metabolism, and elimination.
questions.explanationZh: pharmacokinetics 关注 ADME：吸收、分布、代谢、排泄。

questions.questionEn: Which description best matches pharmacodynamics?
questions.questionZh: pharmacodynamics 最贴近哪种描述？

options.zh: 药物对受体和机体产生的作用
options.en: How the drug acts on receptors and the body
How the body handles the drug

questions.explanationEn: Pharmacodynamics studies what the drug does to the body.
questions.explanationZh: pharmacodynamics 研究药物对身体“做了什么”。

questions.chapter: Chapter 8 — Vascular Access and Medication Administration
questions.questionEn: Which of the following is a parenteral route?
questions.questionZh: 哪一项属于 parenteral route？
questions.explanationEn: Parenteral routes bypass the digestive tract, such as IV, IM, SC, and IO.
questions.explanationZh: parenteral 一般指绕过消化道，如 IV、IM、SC、IO 等。

questions.questionEn: What is a common clinical consideration in geriatric patients?
questions.questionZh: 老年病人的一个常见 clinical consideration 是？

options.en: Their drug responses are always identical
They usually have no baseline illness

options.zh: 可能有多病共存和非典型表现
options.en: They may have multiple comorbidities and atypical presentations

options.zh: 一定能清楚表达全部症状
options.en: They will always clearly express all symptoms

questions.explanationEn: Older adults often have multiple comorbidities, complex medication profiles, and atypical presentations.
questions.explanationZh: 老年患者常有多病共存、用药复杂和症状不典型。

questions.questionEn: Which questioning style usually helps patients describe their complaint more fully?
questions.questionZh: 哪种提问方式通常更有助于病人完整描述主诉？

options.en: Not letting the patient speak freely at all
Interrupting the patient as quickly as possible

questions.explanationEn: Open-ended questions often help patients describe the complaint and illness course more completely.
questions.explanationZh: 开放式问题常帮助病人更完整地表达主诉与病程。

questions.questionEn: Which finding most strongly suggests inadequate ventilation?
questions.questionZh: 哪项最能提示病人可能存在 inadequate 通气？

options.zh: 脉搏规则且无呼吸困难主诉
options.en: A regular pulse with no breathing complaint

options.zh: 单纯血压偏高但呼吸正常
options.en: Isolated elevated blood pressure with normal breathing

options.zh: 说话完整、皮肤温暖、精神清楚
options.en: Full sentences, warm skin, and normal mental status

options.zh: 呼吸浅慢，胸廓起伏不足，意识逐渐变差
options.en: Shallow, slow respirations with poor chest rise and worsening mental status

questions.explanationEn: Inadequate ventilation often presents with insufficient rate or depth, poor chest rise, CO2 retention, and declining mental status.
questions.explanationZh: 通气不足常表现为呼吸频率或深度不足、胸廓起伏差、二氧化碳潴留和意识恶化。

questions.questionEn: During bag-mask ventilation, what best indicates that the technique is effective?
questions.questionZh: 使用 bag-mask 通气 时，什么最能说明操作有效？

options.zh: 面罩漏气明显但操作者感觉轻松
options.en: A large mask leak as long as the operator feels comfortable

options.zh: 可见胸廓适度抬起，且病人氧合/通气指标改善
options.en: Visible moderate chest rise with improving oxygenation and ventilation indicators

options.zh: 挤压越快越好，不管胸廓是否起伏
options.en: Squeezing as fast as possible regardless of chest rise

questions.explanationEn: Effective BVM ventilation is judged by chest rise and clinical improvement, not by squeezing speed or operator impression alone.
questions.explanationZh: 有效 BVM 通气要看胸廓起伏和临床改善，不是看挤压速度或主观感觉。

questions.chapter: Chapter 12 — Expanded EMS Systems and Community Paramedicine in Canada
questions.questionEn: Which patient would most likely benefit from a community paramedicine approach?
questions.questionZh: 哪类病人最可能从 community paramedicine 模式中获益？

options.en: A patient in cardiac arrest requiring active resuscitation
options.zh: 一名心脏骤停、需要积极复苏的病人

options.en: A patient needing immediate surgical intervention for major trauma
options.zh: 一名因严重创伤需要立即外科干预的病人

options.en: A patient requiring no follow-up after discharge
options.zh: 一名出院后完全不需要随访的病人

options.en: A stable patient with repeated 911 calls related to chronic disease management barriers
options.zh: 一名稳定但因慢病管理障碍而反复拨打 911 的病人

questions.explanationEn: Community paramedicine is especially useful for patients with chronic conditions, access barriers, and repeated system use that may be reduced through follow-up and support.
questions.explanationZh: Community paramedicine 特别适合那些有慢性病、就医障碍、且反复使用急救系统、可通过随访和支持改善的病人。

questions.questionEn: What is the normal duration of a full-term pregnancy?
questions.questionZh: 足月妊娠的正常持续时间是多少？

options.en: 44 weeks from the first day of the last menstrual period (LMP)
options.zh: 从末次月经第一天起 44 周

options.en: 40 weeks from the first day of the last menstrual period (LMP)
options.zh: 从末次月经第一天起 40 周

questions.explanationEn: Gestational age is calculated from the first day of the last menstrual period (LMP). Full term is approximately 40 weeks (280 days).
questions.explanationZh: 孕龄从末次月经（LMP）第一天开始计算。足月约为 40 周（280 天）。

questions.questionEn: What are the three stages of labor?
questions.questionZh: 分娩的三个产程是什么？

options.zh: 宫口扩张、胎儿娩出、胎盘娩出
早期产程、活跃产程、恢复期
潜伏期、过渡期、亲子联结

questions.explanationEn: Stage 1: cervical dilation. Stage 2: expulsion of the fetus. Stage 3: delivery of the placenta.
questions.explanationZh: 第一产程：宫颈扩张。第二产程：胎儿娩出。第三产程：胎盘娩出。

questions.questionEn: What is considered a preterm delivery?
questions.questionZh: 什么被认为是早产？
questions.explanationEn: Preterm (premature) delivery is defined as birth before 37 completed weeks of gestation. Preterm infants have higher risk of complications.
questions.explanationZh: 早产定义为孕 37 周前分娩。早产儿并发症风险更高。

questions.questionEn: What is the most common cause of vaginal bleeding in early pregnancy?
questions.questionZh: 早孕期阴道出血最常见的原因是什么？
questions.explanationEn: Spontaneous abortion (miscarriage) is the most common cause of first-trimester bleeding, occurring in 10–20% of known pregnancies.
questions.explanationZh: 自然流产是早孕期出血最常见原因，在已知妊娠中发生率为 10–20%。

questions.questionEn: What is an ectopic pregnancy?
questions.questionZh: 什么是宫外孕？

options.en: Implantation of a fertilized egg outside the uterus, most commonly in a fallopian tube
options.zh: 受精卵在子宫外着床，最常见于输卵管

questions.explanationEn: Ectopic pregnancy occurs when implantation happens outside the uterus. ~95% are tubal. It is life-threatening if rupture occurs.
questions.explanationZh: 宫外孕指受精卵在子宫外着床。约 95% 为输卵管妊娠。破裂时危及生命。

questions.questionEn: What is placenta previa?
questions.questionZh: 什么是前置胎盘？

options.en: Placenta implanted low in the uterus, covering or near the cervical opening
options.zh: 胎盘位置低，覆盖或接近宫颈口

options.en: Premature separation of a normally implanted placenta
options.zh: 正常位置胎盘的过早剥离

questions.explanationEn: Placenta previa means the placenta is implanted over or very near the internal cervical os, causing painless bright red bleeding in the third trimester.
questions.explanationZh: 前置胎盘指胎盘覆盖或非常接近宫颈内口，导致孕晚期无痛性鲜红色出血。

questions.questionEn: What is abruptio placentae (placental abruption)?
questions.questionZh: 什么是胎盘早剥？

options.en: Premature separation of a normally implanted placenta from the uterine wall
options.zh: 正常位置胎盘从子宫壁过早剥离

questions.explanationEn: Abruptio placentae is premature separation of a normally implanted placenta before delivery. It presents with painful bleeding and can cause fetal distress and maternal shock.
questions.explanationZh: 胎盘早剥指正常位置胎盘在分娩前过早剥离。表现为疼痛性出血，可导致胎儿窘迫和产妇休克。

questions.questionEn: What is preeclampsia?
questions.questionZh: 什么是子痫前期？

options.en: High blood pressure and proteinuria after 20 weeks gestation
options.zh: 孕 20 周后出现高血压和蛋白尿

questions.explanationEn: Preeclampsia is defined by new-onset hypertension and proteinuria after 20 weeks. It can progress to eclampsia (seizures) if untreated.
questions.explanationZh: 子痫前期定义为孕 20 周后新发高血压和蛋白尿。未治疗可进展为子痫（抽搐）。

questions.questionEn: What is the most serious complication of preeclampsia?
questions.questionZh: 子痫前期最严重的并发症是什么？
questions.explanationEn: Eclampsia is the onset of seizures in a woman with preeclampsia. It is life-threatening for both mother and fetus.
questions.explanationZh: 子痫是子痫前期孕妇出现抽搐。对母婴均危及生命。

questions.questionEn: What is a prolapsed umbilical cord?
questions.questionZh: 什么是脐带脱垂？

options.en: Umbilical cord wrapped around the baby's neck
Umbilical cord presenting ahead of the fetus, causing compression
options.zh: 脐带先于胎儿出现，导致受压

questions.explanationEn: Prolapsed cord means the cord slips ahead of the presenting part and can be compressed, cutting off fetal oxygen. This is an obstetric emergency requiring immediate delivery.
questions.explanationZh: 脐带脱垂指脐带滑至胎先露部前方，可能被压迫，切断胎儿氧供。这是需要立即分娩的产科急症。

questions.questionEn: What is the first step in neonatal resuscitation after birth?
questions.questionZh: 新生儿出生后复苏的第一步是什么？

options.zh: 擦干、保暖、体位、吸引（刺激）

questions.explanationEn: Initial steps include drying and warming the infant, positioning the airway, clearing secretions if needed, and providing tactile stimulation.
questions.explanationZh: 初始步骤包括擦干和保暖新生儿、体位摆放、必要时清理分泌物，以及提供触觉刺激。

questions.questionEn: What is a normal heart rate for a newborn?
questions.questionZh: 新生儿的正常心率是多少？
questions.explanationEn: A normal newborn heart rate is greater than 100 bpm. Below 100 suggests the need for intervention; below 60 requires chest compressions.
questions.explanationZh: 正常新生儿心率大于 100 次/分。低于 100 提示需要干预；低于 60 需要胸外按压。

questions.questionEn: What is the Apgar score used for?
questions.questionZh: Apgar 评分用于什么？

options.en: To assess the newborn's condition at 1 and 5 minutes after birth
options.zh: 评估新生儿出生后 1 分钟和 5 分钟的状况

questions.explanationEn: The Apgar score evaluates five criteria (appearance, pulse, grimace, activity, respiration) at 1 and 5 minutes to assess the need for resuscitation.
questions.explanationZh: Apgar 评分在 1 和 5 分钟时评估五项指标（肤色、心率、反射、肌张力、呼吸），以评估复苏需求。

questions.questionEn: What are the five components of the Apgar score?
questions.questionZh: Apgar 评分的五个组成部分是什么？

options.zh: 肤色、心率、反射、肌张力、呼吸
肌张力、反射、肤色、呼吸、喂养
气道、呼吸、循环、神志、暴露

options.en: Heart rate, oxygen saturation, temperature, weight, length
options.zh: 心率、血氧、体温、体重、身长

questions.explanationEn: Apgar: Appearance (color), Pulse (heart rate), Grimace (reflex irritability), Activity (muscle tone), Respiration (breathing effort).
questions.explanationZh: Apgar：肤色、心率、反射、肌张力、呼吸。

questions.questionEn: What is the compression-to-ventilation ratio for neonatal CPR?
questions.questionZh: 新生儿 CPR 的按压通气比是多少？
questions.explanationEn: Neonatal CPR uses a 3:1 ratio: 3 compressions followed by 1 ventilation, aiming for 120 events per minute (90 compressions + 30 breaths).
questions.explanationZh: 新生儿 CPR 使用 3:1 比例：3 次按压后 1 次通气，目标每分钟 120 个事件（90 次按压 + 30 次呼吸）。

questions.questionEn: What is meconium?
questions.questionZh: 什么是胎粪？

options.en: The first stool of a newborn, composed of materials ingested in utero
options.zh: 新生儿的第一次大便，由宫内吞咽的物质组成

questions.explanationEn: Meconium is the thick, dark green or black first stool. Meconium-stained amniotic fluid may indicate fetal distress.
questions.explanationZh: 胎粪是浓稠的深绿色或黑色第一次大便。胎粪染色的羊水可能提示胎儿窘迫。

questions.questionEn: When is suctioning indicated for a newborn with meconium-stained fluid?
questions.questionZh: 胎粪染色羊水的新生儿何时需要吸引？

options.en: Only if the baby is not vigorous (poor tone, effort, or heart rate)
options.zh: 仅当婴儿不活跃时（肌张力差、呼吸弱或心率低）

options.en: Only if the fluid is thick

questions.explanationEn: Current guidelines recommend suctioning only if the baby is not vigorous. Routine suctioning of vigorous babies is no longer recommended.
questions.explanationZh: 当前指南仅建议在婴儿不活跃时吸引。不再推荐对活跃婴儿常规吸引。

questions.questionEn: What is the purpose of delayed cord clamping?
questions.questionZh: 延迟脐带结扎的目的是什么？

options.en: To allow placental transfusion, improving iron stores and blood volume
options.zh: 允许胎盘输血，改善铁储备和血容量

questions.explanationEn: Delaying cord clamping for 30–60 seconds (if the baby is stable) allows additional blood transfer from the placenta, improving hemoglobin and iron levels.
questions.explanationZh: 延迟脐带结扎 30–60 秒（如果婴儿稳定）可允许额外的胎盘血液转移，改善血红蛋白和铁水平。

questions.questionEn: What is the most common cause of cardiac arrest in children?
questions.questionZh: 儿童心脏骤停最常见的原因是什么？

options.en: Respiratory failure or shock leading to hypoxia
options.zh: 呼吸衰竭或休克导致的缺氧

questions.explanationEn: Unlike adults, pediatric cardiac arrest is usually secondary to respiratory failure or shock, not primary cardiac events. Early airway and breathing support is critical.
questions.explanationZh: 与成人不同，儿童心脏骤停通常继发于呼吸衰竭或休克，而非原发心脏事件。早期气道和呼吸支持至关重要。

questions.questionEn: What is the compression-to-ventilation ratio for pediatric CPR with two rescuers?
questions.questionZh: 两名施救者儿童 CPR 的按压通气比是多少？
questions.explanationEn: For pediatric CPR with two rescuers, use 15:2 ratio. Single rescuer uses 30:2 (same as adult).
questions.explanationZh: 两名施救者儿童 CPR 使用 15:2 比例。单人施救使用 30:2（与成人相同）。

questions.questionEn: How deep should chest compressions be in an infant?
questions.questionZh: 婴儿胸外按压应多深？

options.en: At least one-third the depth of the chest (about 4 cm or 1.5 inches)
options.zh: 至少胸廓深度的三分之一（约 4 cm 或 1.5 英寸）

questions.explanationEn: For infants, compress at least one-third the anterior-posterior diameter of the chest, approximately 4 cm (1.5 inches).
questions.explanationZh: 婴儿按压至少胸廓前后径的三分之一，约 4 cm（1.5 英寸）。

questions.questionEn: How deep should chest compressions be in a child?
questions.questionZh: 儿童胸外按压应多深？

options.en: At least one-third the depth of the chest (about 5 cm or 2 inches)
options.zh: 至少胸廓深度的三分之一（约 5 cm 或 2 英寸）

questions.explanationEn: For children, compress at least one-third the anterior-posterior diameter, approximately 5 cm (2 inches).
questions.explanationZh: 儿童按压至少胸廓前后径的三分之一，约 5 cm（2 英寸）。

questions.questionEn: What is the most common cause of airway obstruction in an unconscious child?
questions.questionZh: 无意识儿童气道梗阻最常见的原因是什么？
questions.explanationEn: In unconscious children, the tongue often falls back and obstructs the airway. Proper head positioning (head-tilt-chin-lift or jaw thrust) is essential.
questions.explanationZh: 无意识儿童中，舌头常后坠阻塞气道。正确的头部定位（仰头抬颏或推颌）至关重要。

questions.questionEn: What is croup (laryngotracheobronchitis)?
questions.questionZh: 什么是喉炎（喉气管支气管炎）？

options.en: A bacterial infection of the epiglottis
A viral infection causing upper airway swelling, barky cough, and stridor
options.zh: 病毒感染导致上气道肿胀、犬吠样咳嗽和喘鸣

questions.explanationEn: Croup is a viral upper airway infection common in young children, characterized by barky (seal-like) cough, stridor, and respiratory distress.
questions.explanationZh: 喉炎是幼儿常见的病毒性上气道感染，特征为犬吠样咳嗽、喘鸣和呼吸窘迫。

questions.questionEn: What is epiglottitis?
questions.questionZh: 什么是会厌炎？

options.zh: 引起舌头肿胀的过敏反应

options.en: A life-threatening bacterial infection causing rapid swelling of the epiglottis
options.zh: 危及生命的细菌感染，导致会厌快速肿胀

questions.explanationEn: Epiglottitis is a bacterial infection (often H. influenzae type b) causing rapid epiglottic swelling. Patients present with drooling, difficulty swallowing, high fever, and tripod positioning. Do not examine the throat; this can trigger complete obstruction.
questions.explanationZh: 会厌炎是细菌感染（常为 B 型流感嗜血杆菌），导致会厌快速肿胀。患者表现为流涎、吞咽困难、高热和三脚架体位。不要检查咽喉；这可能触发完全梗阻。

questions.questionEn: What is a febrile seizure?
questions.questionZh: 什么是热性惊厥？

options.en: A seizure caused by brain tumor
A seizure triggered by rapid rise in body temperature, common in children 6 months to 5 years
options.zh: 体温快速升高触发的惊厥，常见于 6 个月至 5 岁儿童

questions.explanationEn: Febrile seizures occur with fever (usually >38°C/100.4°F) in children 6 months to 5 years. Most are brief and self-limited, but evaluation is needed to rule out serious infection.
questions.explanationZh: 热性惊厥发生于发热（通常 >38°C/100.4°F）的 6 个月至 5 岁儿童。大多数短暂且自限，但需要评估以排除严重感染。

questions.chapter: Chapter 2 — The Well-Being of the Paramedic
questions.questionEn: What is one of the most common sources of stress in the paramedic profession?
questions.questionZh: Paramedic职业中最常见的压力来源是什么？

options.zh: 不规律的工作时间和轮班
options.en: Irregular work hours and shift work

questions.explanationEn: Chapter 2 emphasizes that irregular hours, shift work, and long duty periods are major sources of stress in paramedicine, affecting sleep, family life, and physical health.
questions.explanationZh: Chapter 2 强调，不规律的工作时间、轮班制和长时间工作是paramedic职业压力的主要来源之一，会影响睡眠、家庭生活和身体健康。

questions.chapter: Chapter 2 — The Well-Being of the Paramedic
questions.questionEn: What is the most accurate understanding of Critical Incident Stress?
questions.questionZh: 关于Critical Incident Stress（危机事件压力），最准确的理解是什么？

options.zh: 它是软弱的表现，应该隐藏
options.en: It is a sign of weakness and should be hidden

options.zh: 它是对异常事件的正常心理反应
options.en: It is a normal psychological response to abnormal events

options.zh: 它会在24小时内自动消失

questions.explanationEn: Chapter 2 clearly states that Critical Incident Stress is a normal psychological and physiological response to abnormal, traumatic events—not a sign of weakness—and requires appropriate coping and support.
questions.explanationZh: Chapter 2 明确指出，Critical Incident Stress是对异常、创伤性事件的正常心理和生理反应，不是软弱的标志，需要适当的应对和支持。

questions.chapter: Chapter 2 — The Well-Being of the Paramedic
questions.questionEn: What is the core principle of Standard Precautions?
questions.questionZh: Standard Precautions（标准预防措施）的核心原则是什么？

options.zh: 只在确认患者有传染病时才使用防护
options.en: Use protection only when the patient is confirmed infectious

options.zh: 将所有患者的血液和体液视为潜在传染源
options.en: Treat all blood and body fluids from all patients as potentially infectious

questions.explanationEn: Chapter 2 emphasizes that the core of Standard Precautions is treating all blood, body fluids, secretions, and excretions from all patients as potentially infectious, regardless of known infection status.
questions.explanationZh: Chapter 2 强调Standard Precautions的核心是将所有患者的血液、体液、分泌物和排泄物视为潜在传染源，无论患者是否有已知感染。

questions.chapter: Chapter 2 — The Well-Being of the Paramedic
questions.questionEn: What is the main difference between burnout and acute stress?
questions.questionZh: Burnout（职业倦怠）与急性压力的主要区别是什么？

options.zh: Burnout是慢性的、累积的疲惫状态
options.en: Burnout is a chronic, cumulative state of exhaustion

options.zh: Burnout是短期的，急性压力是长期的
options.en: Burnout is short-term, acute stress is long-term

questions.explanationEn: Chapter 2 distinguishes acute stress (response to a single event) from burnout (chronic emotional, physical, and mental exhaustion from prolonged exposure to job stressors).
questions.explanationZh: Chapter 2 区分了急性压力（对单一事件的反应）和burnout（长期暴露于工作压力导致的慢性情绪、身体和心理疲惫）。

questions.chapter: Chapter 2 — The Well-Being of the Paramedic
questions.questionEn: What should be the first step after a needlestick injury?
questions.questionZh: 针刺伤（needlestick injury）后的正确处理步骤首先应该是什么？

options.en: Go to the emergency room immediately
Soak the wound in alcohol for 10 minutes
Wash the wound with soap and water

questions.explanationEn: Chapter 2 clearly states that after a needlestick injury, immediately wash the wound with soap and water, then report it promptly and seek medical evaluation and possible post-exposure prophylaxis.
questions.explanationZh: Chapter 2 明确指出，针刺伤后应立即用肥皂和水清洗伤口，然后尽快报告并寻求医疗评估和可能的预防性治疗。

questions.chapter: Chapter 2 — The Well-Being of the Paramedic
questions.questionEn: What is the most important recognition about sleep's impact on paramedic performance?
questions.questionZh: 关于睡眠对paramedic表现的影响，最重要的认识是什么？

options.zh: Paramedics可以通过咖啡因完全补偿睡眠不足
options.en: Paramedics can fully compensate for sleep loss with caffeine

options.zh: 睡眠不足会严重损害决策能力和反应时间
options.en: Sleep deprivation significantly impairs decision-making and reaction time

options.zh: 只有连续48小时不睡才会有影响
options.en: Only 48 hours without sleep has an impact

options.zh: 睡眠不足只影响情绪，不影响判断
options.en: Sleep deprivation only affects mood, not judgment

questions.explanationEn: Chapter 2 emphasizes that sleep deprivation significantly impairs cognitive function, judgment, reaction time, and technical skills, posing a major risk to patient and personal safety.
questions.explanationZh: Chapter 2 强调睡眠不足会严重影响认知功能、判断力、反应时间和操作技能，是患者安全和个人安全的重大风险因素。

questions.chapter: Chapter 2 — The Well-Being of the Paramedic
questions.questionEn: What is the primary purpose of CISD (Critical Incident Stress Debriefing)?
questions.questionZh: CISD（Critical Incident Stress Debriefing）的主要目的是什么？

options.zh: 帮助团队成员处理和理解对创伤事件的反应
options.en: Help team members process and understand reactions to traumatic events

questions.explanationEn: Chapter 2 explains that CISD is a structured group discussion process designed to help those involved in critical incidents share experiences, understand reactions, reduce stress, and promote recovery.
questions.explanationZh: Chapter 2 解释CISD是一个结构化的小组讨论过程，旨在帮助参与危机事件的人员分享经历、理解反应、减少压力并促进恢复。

questions.chapter: Chapter 2 — The Well-Being of the Paramedic
questions.questionEn: What is the most important principle regarding Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) use?
questions.questionZh: 个人防护装备（PPE）的使用原则，最重要的是什么？

options.zh: 根据预期暴露风险选择合适的PPE
options.en: Select appropriate PPE based on anticipated exposure risks

options.zh: 只在医院要求时才使用
options.en: Use only when required by the hospital

options.zh: 只在看起来脏的患者身上使用
options.en: Use only with visibly dirty patients

options.zh: PPE会妨碍工作效率，应尽量少用
options.en: PPE hinders efficiency and should be minimized

questions.explanationEn: Chapter 2 emphasizes selecting and using appropriate levels of PPE based on the anticipated risk of exposure to blood, body fluids, or other infectious materials—key to protecting yourself and patients.
questions.explanationZh: Chapter 2 强调应根据预期的血液、体液或其他传染物质暴露风险，选择和使用合适级别的PPE，这是保护自己和患者的关键。

questions.questionEn: What is the core goal of Primary Prevention?
questions.questionZh: Primary Prevention（一级预防）的核心目标是什么？

options.en: Treat diseases that have already occurred

options.zh: 防止疾病或伤害的发生
options.en: Prevent disease or injury from occurring

questions.explanationEn: Chapter 3 defines Primary Prevention as strategies to prevent disease or injury from occurring in the first place, such as vaccination, safety education, and environmental modifications.
questions.explanationZh: Chapter 3 定义Primary Prevention为防止疾病或伤害首次发生的策略，如疫苗接种、安全教育和环境改善。

questions.questionEn: What does the Haddon Matrix emphasize regarding motor vehicle crash prevention?
questions.questionZh: 关于车祸预防，Haddon Matrix 强调什么？

options.zh: 从事件前、事件中、事件后三个阶段系统分析预防策略
options.en: Systematically analyze prevention strategies across pre-event, event, and post-event phases

questions.explanationEn: Chapter 3 presents the Haddon Matrix as a systematic framework for analyzing injuries, dividing prevention strategies into pre-event (prevention), event (injury reduction), and post-event (outcome improvement) phases.
questions.explanationZh: Chapter 3 介绍Haddon Matrix作为分析伤害的系统框架，将预防策略分为事件前（prevention）、事件中（injury reduction）和事件后（outcome improvement）三个阶段。

questions.questionEn: What is the most typical example of Secondary Prevention?
questions.questionZh: Secondary Prevention（二级预防）最典型的例子是什么？
questions.explanationEn: Chapter 3 explains that Secondary Prevention focuses on early detection and prompt intervention, such as hypertension screening and cancer screening, aiming to identify and treat conditions before they become severe.
questions.explanationZh: Chapter 3 解释Secondary Prevention针对早期检测和及时干预，如高血压筛查、癌症早筛等，目标是在症状严重前发现和治疗。

questions.questionEn: What is the primary goal of Tertiary Prevention?
questions.questionZh: Tertiary Prevention（三级预防）的主要目标是什么？

options.zh: 减少已发生疾病或伤害的长期影响和并发症
options.en: Reduce long-term effects and complications of existing disease or injury

questions.explanationEn: Chapter 3 defines Tertiary Prevention as reducing long-term adverse consequences of existing disease or injury, such as post-stroke rehabilitation and chronic disease management.
questions.explanationZh: Chapter 3 定义Tertiary Prevention为减少已发生疾病或伤害的长期不良后果，如卒中后康复、慢性病管理等。
